Abuse is presumed if that five-year figure reaches a threshold. The threshold is 25% of your nonpriority unsecured debt, but never less than $10,275 and never more than $17,150.

With $30,000 of nonpriority unsecured debt, 25% is $7,500, so $10,275 applies, and abuse is presumed if at least $171.25 a month is left after allowed expenses ($10,275 ÷ 60). With $80,000 of that debt, 25% is $20,000, so the $17,150 cap applies, and the monthly line is about $285.83 ($17,150 ÷ 60).

Say you have $30,000 of nonpriority unsecured debt. A 25% share is $7,500, which is below $10,275, so the threshold is $10,275. Divided by 60 months, $10,275 is $171.25 a month left after allowed expenses. With $80,000 of that debt, a 25% share is $20,000. The $20,000 share is above $17,150, so the threshold is $17,150, or about $285.83 a month.

- debts from fraud or defalcation while acting as a fiduciary, or from embezzlement or larceny
